subject: Core Mathematics
topic: Area of a Part of a Circle

unit.substrand: Sub-Strand 2.6: Area of a Part of a Circle
unit.sep: Decompose plane regions, justify proportional area models, calculate and verify geometry.
unit.careers: Illustrative applications in design, material planning and landscape layout; no qualification claims.
unit.focus: Identify annuli, sectors, annular sectors, segments and circle overlaps, then justify their areas.
unit.phenomenon: A paper design team gets conflicting area estimates because each person shades a different region.
unit.supportingPhenomena: Ring paths, sector allocations, chord-cut segments and intersecting-circle designs.
unit.drivingQuestion: How can we identify the exact region before choosing an area calculation? KICD: How do we use the concept of the area of a part of a circle in real life?
unit.storylineThread: Annulus → applications → sectors → reverse angle → annular sector → minor/major segments → equal/unequal overlap → project → critique → independent transfer.
unit.coreCompetencies:
Creativity and Imagination: the learner makes an improvised dartboard of different numbers of concentric circles.
Learning to Learn: the learner draws illustrations of two intersecting circles to identify the common area/part between the two circles.
Communication and collaboration: the learners engage to improvise locally available materials to make dartboards and beaded necklaces.
unit.values:
Responsibility: the learner makes dartboard of different numbers of concentric circles from the immediate environment
Unity: the learner collaborates in a group and uses paper cutouts to make sectors of circles to determine their areas as part of a circle
unit.pcis:
Parental Engagement and Empowerment: the learner engages parents in using locally available materials for making improvised beaded necklaces.
Environmental Education: the learner sources locally available materials to make necklaces and dartboards.
Learner Support Programmes (Peer Education): the learner works with others to make necklaces using beading techniques of different coloured annular sectors.
unit.content: Area of an annulus; Area of a sector of a circle; Area of an annular sector; Area of a segment; Area of common region between two intersecting circles; Application on the use of the area of a part of a circle

assessment.subjectLabel: AREA OF A PART OF A CIRCLE
assessment.instructions: Lesson 12,40 minutes including 3 minutes procedure and 4 minutes final checking. Work independently with CM212 and a scientific calculator in degree mode. Show a labelled region/decomposition and an exact area expression; approximate to 3 decimal places where requested. Formula support on CM212 is allowed; no teaching cards. Use square units. Project participation/use exploration also has formative evidence in Lessons 10–11; this written task does not certify physical making skills.

sections.title: 1. Ring area and a check
sections.prompt: Find annulus A area exactly. Explain why the difference of squared radii is appropriate and verify by recombining with the inner disk.
sections.exemplar: π(8²−5²)=39π cm²;39π+25π=64π restores the outer disk. Both circular boundaries share a centre; subtract the inner disk, not a disk of radius 8−5.

sections.title: 2. Sector and annular-sector comparison
sections.prompt: Find B and C areas exactly and explain the difference between the two decompositions. Check that adding C to the matching radius 6 sector restores B.
sections.exemplar: B=(80/360)π9²=18π cm². C=(80/360)π(81−36)=10π cm². Matching radius 6 sector 8π;10π+8π=18π. The hole removes the smaller sector with the same centre and angle.

sections.title: 3. Minor segment
sections.prompt: Find D’s minor-segment area exactly and approximately. Explain the triangle subtraction and check that the result is positive and less than the sector.
sections.exemplar: Sector 25π cm²; right central triangle 50 cm²; segment 25π−50≈28.540 cm². The chord bounds a region outside the triangle but within the 90° sector.0<25π−50<25π.

sections.title: 4. Intersecting-circle overlap
sections.prompt: Find E’s common area exactly and approximately. Explain why two segment areas are added and why doubling is valid in this case. State a size check.
sections.exemplar: Each segment(60/360)π36−(1/2)36 sin 60°=6π−9√3. Overlap 12π−18√3≈6.522 cm². The common chord divides the lens into congruent segments because equal radii/central angles give equal geometry. It is positive and less than one 36π cm² disk.

sections.title: 5. Explore a safe design use
sections.prompt: Choose A or C as a proposed paper ornament. Explain what its computed area would estimate, one benefit of that estimate and one further datum/assumption needed for real material planning. Describe one safe next step to explore the proposed use. This is a written plan; no physical making is required.
sections.exemplar: For C,10π cm² estimates the planar area of one ornament piece. It can help compare intended material quantities, but cutting waste, joining allowance and thickness are not included. A safe next step is a labelled paper template using the stated radii/angle with teacher-approved tools. Accept a similarly justified annulus example. Do not infer actual practical skill from the written plan.

rubric.excellent: All three exact areas, matching-region explanations and recombination checks are correct and clearly labelled.
rubric.proficient: Correct areas and decompositions with valid recombination checks and square units.
rubric.developing: Some correct model/area work but a radius, angle fraction, subtraction or unit needs correction.
rubric.belowExpectations: Needs guided region identification before selecting a formula.

rubric.criterion: Determine and justify a minor-segment area
rubric.excellent: Correct exact/approximate result, triangle explanation and both size checks, supported by a clear diagram.
rubric.proficient: Correct sector-minus-triangle result and explanation with a valid size check.
rubric.developing: Identifies the sector/triangle but a calculation, subtraction or explanation is incomplete.
rubric.belowExpectations: Needs guided support to distinguish the segment from the sector or triangle.

rubric.criterion: Determine and justify the common area of intersecting circles
rubric.excellent: Correct exact/approximate area with a clear two-segment decomposition, valid symmetry explanation and size check.
rubric.proficient: Correct overlap calculation and explanation of why the two equal segments can be doubled here.
rubric.developing: Some correct segment reasoning but calculation, symmetry condition or interpretation needs correction.
rubric.belowExpectations: Needs guided work to identify the intersection and its component segments.

rubric.criterion: Explain and explore a practical use with limits
rubric.excellent: Connects the selected area to a specific benefit, relevant omitted factor and safe concrete next step without overclaiming the model.
rubric.proficient: Explains a relevant use, benefit, limitation and safe exploration step.
rubric.developing: A relevant use is proposed but the quantity, limitation or next step is vague.
rubric.belowExpectations: Needs prompts to connect the planar area to a usable design estimate.
